correctness.rationale: The lattice M is explicitly the index-eight parity sublattice of Z^7. The 16 network vertices obey 12 complete facet inequalities, obtained by gluing the three even-parity tetrahedra along their common edges of a tree; their 12 facets each have 12 affinely spanning vertices. The exact included program computes all 711 face intersections and saturated intrinsic normal cones; every nonsmooth face lies inside four maximal nonsmooth 4-faces fixing an internal edge to 0 or 1. Each maximal singular normal cone has four primitive rays in rank 3 forming a unit-square relation, giving transverse ab-cd=0. Face lattices are unimodular Delta1 x Delta3 and cross-edge intersections Delta1 x Delta1. Orbit-face duality proves all support components and intersection incidence, and Segre degree gives 16. Semigroup monomial inclusion-exclusion in positive degree proves the Hilbert formula, with degree-zero correction. The bundled exact lattice checker returns VERIFY_OK, confirms all enumerative lemmas and compares monomial counts through degree three. The all-degree proof does not rely on finite numerics. Limitations: only reduced singular locus, not Jacobian scheme, no local claim at intersection points.

originality.rationale: Compared exact model, singular-support statement, orbit-closure components, pairwise incidence, transverse cone, and Hilbert series—not title coincidence. Primary Sturmfels–Sullivant 2004 constructs phylogenetic toric ideals; Buczyńska–Wiśniewski 2006 proves network-fan properties, resolutions and terminal Gorenstein structure, including a four-leaf conifold example. They supply prior general techniques but do not state the four components and cycle incidence of the five-leaf reduced singular locus nor its complete homogeneous Hilbert series. Buczyńska 2010 concerns graph extensions. The current small-model database lists five-leaf CFN dimension 7 degree 44 but leaves singular dimension/degree blank; it has no equivalent table. Scientific-record semantic and literature keyword searches did not return a covering result. General methods may allow an implicit specialization; searched literature cannot prove absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The singular locus of a CFN phylogenetic toric variety is a natural measure of model degeneracy, and a live comparison table explicitly tracks this invariant but has no data for the five-leaf model. The theorem determines the entire reduced support, equidimensional codimension-three geometry, four Segre fourfolds of degree four, complete cycle incidence and transverse nodes, and all graded Hilbert dimensions; these distinguish it from routine singular-point counts or a re-expression of general terminality. The Hilbert series degree-zero correction carries genuine incidence information. The model is the smallest trivalent-tree case with two interior edges, so the two-edge interaction is mathematically motivated. Scope limited to one five-leaf topology and reduced structure.
